decision.summary: The Fed raised its policy rate by 25 basis points, to 4.5% to 4.75%. The vote was 12-0.

changes.quote: Inflation has eased somewhat but remains elevated.
changes.explanation: New language added in this statement.

changes.quote: Russia's war against Ukraine is causing tremendous human and economic hardship and is contributing to elevated global uncertainty.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “Russia's war against Ukraine is causing tremendous human and economic hardship.”

changes.quote: Inflation remains elevated, reflecting supply and demand imbalances related to the pandemic, higher food and energy prices, and broader price pressures.
changes.explanation: Language from the previous statement that was dropped.

changes.quote: The war and related events are contributing to upward pressure on inflation and are weighing on global economic activity.
changes.explanation: Language from the previous statement that was dropped.

changes.quote: In support of these goals, the Committee decided to raise the target range for the federal funds rate to 4-1/2 to 4-3/4 percent.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “In support of these goals, the Committee decided to raise the target range for the federal funds rate to 4-1/4 to 4-1/2 percent.”

changes.quote: In determining the extent of future increases in the target range, the Committee will take into account the cumulative tightening of monetary policy, the lags with which monetary policy affects economic activity and inflation, and economic and financial developments.
changes.explanation: New language added in this statement.

tone_quotes.quote: In support of these goals, the Committee decided to raise the target range for the federal funds rate to 4-1/2 to 4-3/4 percent.

The Committee anticipates that ongoing increases in the target range will be appropriate in order to attain a stance of monetary policy that is sufficiently restrictive to return inflation to 2 percent over time.
The Committee is strongly committed to returning inflation to its 2 percent objective.

for_you.text: On a $5,000 card balance at about 16.27% APR, a 25 bp increase raises monthly interest by about $1.04.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury yield, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 3.39% and moved -13 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 6.15% would fall by about $25.17 a month.
High-yield savings rates usually follow the Fed partly; on $10,000 that means roughly $15.00 a year more in interest.
Unemployment was 3.5%, and employers added an average of 253k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 6.4% over the past year (December 2022); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 5.1%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 2.7% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved -12 bp on the day, and the S&P 500 moved 1.05%.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved -0.3% on the day.

whats_next: The dictionary tone reading is hawkish (leaning toward higher rates). The forecast model gave the next meeting: hold 11%, cut 0%, hike 88%.
